# Score-Based Diffusion: Reading Guide {.unnumbered}

These tutorials are written for undergraduates with no prior SDE background.
Read them in order. The numbers below identify the four parts of this series.

| Order | Tutorial | Teaching question | Longer derivations, kept as subsections |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Learning the Score: VP Diffusion from First Principles](./25-learning-the-score.qmd) | How do we learn an unknown marginal score from a known corruption process? | Gaussian increments and expected Taylor step; VP moments and Gaussian kernel; posterior averaging and MSE proof; optional stochastic-integral derivation |
| 2 | [Probability-Flow Sampling: From Density Evolution to Samples](./26-probability-flow-sampling.qmd) | Why does the score give a sampling velocity, and how do we use it? | Probability flux, Gaussian smoothing and Fokker–Planck; probability-flow construction; quantile maps; optional integration-by-parts and reverse-SDE checks |
| 3 | [Diffusion, Neural ODEs, and Normalizing Flows](./27-diffusion-neural-odes-normalizing-flows.qmd) | What connects diffusion sampling to invertible transport and density estimation? | Continuous change of variables; Gaussian flow and coupling comparison; likelihood identity; conditional velocity regression and its score connection |
| 4 | [Langevin Dynamics](./28-langevin-dynamics.qmd) | How does fixed-target sampling differ from reverse diffusion? | Gaussian moments and ULA bias; stationarity; time-scaling ratio; transport-plus-Langevin decomposition |

Each tutorial has a core reading route, worked examples, and derivation
subsections. Advanced proofs are labelled optional. Topic ownership is explicit:
Tutorial 1 proves the corruption and learning identities; Tutorial 2 derives
density evolution and sampling; Tutorial 3 develops transport and likelihood; Tutorial 4 connects fixed-target
Langevin sampling to diffusion and annealing.

## Prerequisite ladder and reading route

| Stage | New material | Where introduced |
|---|---|---|
| Entry | Elementary derivatives, Taylor expansion, ODEs, Gaussian algebra, independence, Bayes' rule | Assumed; no stochastic calculus or PDE course required |
| Random steps | Random variable versus realization, Gaussian increments, square-root step scaling, Euler–Maruyama | Tutorial 1: From Gaussian random steps to an SDE |
| Corruption law | Expected Taylor step, mean/variance equations, Gaussian sums | Tutorial 1: Construct the variance-preserving corruption law |
| Learning | Conditional expectation, tower property, posterior weights, MSE-optimality proof | Tutorial 1: Learn an unknown score from known targets |
| Density dynamics | Particle versus population, flux, partial derivatives, divergence, Laplacian, Fokker–Planck | Tutorial 2: Describe motion of an entire density |
| Sampling | Probability-flow velocity, backward steps, cutoff and terminal-prior errors | Tutorial 2: Construct the velocity and generate backward |
| Transport | Jacobian volume scaling, invertibility, density change, couplings and likelihood | Tutorial 3 |
| Equilibrium sampling | Langevin balance, invariance versus convergence, finite-step bias, annealing | Tutorial 4 |

The published [From Local Arrows](./22-vector-fields-to-score-diffusion.qmd)
and [Sampling with Scores](./24-sampling-with-scores.qmd) are
optional geometric background, not substitutes for the SDE introduction here.
The [score-flow lab](../materials/score-flow-lab.html) accompanies the
Gaussian and two-point examples.

**First reading:** follow the four tutorials' core routes and attempt the
understanding checks before opening the answers. In Tutorial 1, skip the
stochastic-integral subsection. In Tutorial 2, the Gaussian-smoothing derivation
provides the main intuition; the integration-by-parts proof and stochastic
sampler can be a second pass. In Tutorial 3, the infinitesimal determinant and
flow-matching proofs are enrichment. The remaining main arguments do not
require those proofs. Tutorial 4 uses only the SDE and density tools from
Tutorials 1–2; it can also be read directly after Tutorial 2. Its density-operator
calculation is optional. Its reverse-diffusion comparison uses the
[reverse-SDE check in Tutorial 2](./26-probability-flow-sampling.qmd#reverse-sde).

The complete MSE proof is now inside Tutorial 1. The existing
[Tweedie tutorial](./23-tweedie-bayes-denoising.qmd) remains a
separate statistical treatment for additional practice.

## Shared notation

| Symbol | Meaning throughout the series |
|---|---|
| $X_t$, $x$ | Random state and a particular observed value, respectively |
| $\epsilon$, $\xi_k$ | Corruption noise and independent numerical-step noise |
| $p_t$, $s_t=\nabla_x\log p_t$ | Forward-noised density and its marginal score |
| $s_\theta$ | Learned score approximation |
| $f(x,t)$, $g(t)$ | Forward-SDE drift and scalar, time-dependent noise amplitude |
| $\alpha_t$, $\sigma_t$ | Signal coefficient and conditional noise standard deviation |
| $v(x,t)=f-\tfrac12g^2s_t$ | Forward-time probability-flow velocity |
| $\Psi_{s\to t}$ | Flow map between specified times |
| $\Phi$ | Standard normal CDF, never a flow map |
| $\tau=T-t$ | Increasing generation clock |
| $u$, $q_u$ | Fixed-target Langevin time and current sampler density |
| $p_\sigma$ | Smoothed law indexed by noise standard deviation in Tutorial 4 |
| $\varrho$ | Mixture-component standard deviation |

Every numerical step magnitude is positive. A forward update uses $+h v$;
a backward update uses $-h v$. On a descending grid, $h_k=t_k-t_{k-1}>0$.
This local convention differs from the signed-step notation in some older notes.
The conditional noise variance $\sigma_t^2$ is distinguished from total marginal
variance, and exact sampling from $p_T$ from its Gaussian approximation.

## Relationship to the existing course notes

The published notes 22, 24, and 23 provide geometric intuition, introductory
worked sampling, and standalone statistical denoising, respectively. This
series is the next derivation sequence: learning → sampling → connections → equilibrium sampling.
It does not replace those notes. The existing broad
[probability-flow perspective](./07-probability-flow-ode.qmd)
can remain an alternative overview alongside this sequence.
